extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers and malaria immunology / systems-biology researchers (PI, co-investigators, lab staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Research-strategy text from an NIH-style R01 proposal describing aims, methods, class definitions, sample handling, statistical thresholds, and modeling approaches to identify correlates of clinical and sterile immunity to Plasmodium falciparum in a pediatric Mali cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical immunity class definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinically immune defined as ≤2 malaria episodes over 3 years; susceptible defined as ≥4 episodes over 3 years; children with 3 episodes are indeterminate and excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes used for analysis: A (Clinically Immune, Uninfected), B (Clinically Immune, Infected), C (Susceptible, Uninfected), D (Susceptible, Infected). Sample counts and available biospecimens are listed in Table 1; class reclassification from prior study described to allow combined analyses (A+B vs C+D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterile immunity (apparently sterile immunity) class definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparent sterile immunity defined as negative Pf PCR at every 2-week surveillance and passive (sick) visit during the season AND boosting of antibodies to ≥1 Pf pre-erythrocytic antigen or An. gambiae gSG6 during the first malaria season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class E (apparently sterile immunity) and Class F (non-protected) are used in sterile-immunity analyses; sample availability by time point is specified (baseline T0 PBMC, whole-blood RNA, plasma; bi-weekly timepoints: whole-blood RNA, plasma, DBS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case definition for a malaria episode
rubrics_metrics.description: Malaria episode defined as axillary temperature >37.5°C and parasite density by blood smear >500 asexual parasites/μl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold chosen to balance sensitivity in diagnosis with specificity in semi-immune populations where fevers may arise from other pathogens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant exclusion criteria affecting malaria risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects with hemoglobin genotypes HbS/C and subjects co-infected with Schistosoma haematobium are excluded from the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other erythrocyte variants will be controlled for (ABO typing performed; genotyping for common α-thalassemia and G6PD variants planned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-interrogation of baseline samples by ultrasensitive qPCR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an ultrasensitive quantitative real-time PCR assay targeting the TARE-2 repeat region with sensitivity of 0.03–0.12 parasites/μl (10–30x more sensitive than original ~1 parasite/μl assay) to verify baseline Pf infection status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gDNA extracted from cryopreserved cell pellets (~200 μl whole blood) will be re-tested to detect occult/low-density parasitemia that might have misclassified subjects as uninfected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pf-specific IgG measurement by protein microarray
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure Pf-specific IgG responses using a protein microarray of 1,087 recombinant Pf antigens (Felgner array).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows single-antigen, stage-specific, or general assessments. Differential reactivity between classes assessed using empirical Bayes methods in the limma package; longitudinal kinetics used to infer incident exposure (T1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of incident exposure (T1) from antibody kinetics
rubrics_metrics.description: T1 is approximated as the 2-week timepoint showing the first significant increase in the sum intensity of antibody responses to pre-erythrocytic antigens (e.g., CSP, TRAP, LSA-1) from baseline (T0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples from documented infected subjects (Class F) serve as controls, where T1 is expected around the time of incident infection. Use fingerprick specimens collected bi-weekly; limited by 2-week temporal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-blood transcriptomics laboratory methods
rubrics_metrics.description: RNA-seq from fingerprick whole-blood collected directly in Tempus; total RNA extraction with rRNA and globin removal using Globin-Zero rRNA Gold kit; library prep targeting 25 million paired-end 2x75 bp reads per sample; sequencing on NextSeq 500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples randomized and processed together to avoid batch effects; reads mapped to human reference (hg38); count data used for differential expression analysis. Timepoints from same child processed together when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential gene expression thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary criteria: genes with absolute fold-change >1.5 and false discovery rate (FDR) <5% will be considered differentially expressed (DEGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power calculations in Table 3 are provided for detecting genes with ≥2-fold change at nominal FDR 5%; smaller sample sizes limit power and comparisons involving small classes (e.g., A, E) are exploratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific analysis tools and gene-set testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Differential expression analysis will use edgeR, DESeq2, and limma-voom; geneset testing via roast and camera (limma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust for baseline covariates (e.g., age) as needed. Confirm selected gene expression results by qPCR and use Ingenuity pathway analysis and modular analysis for downstream interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sample-size considerations / interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Power estimates (Table 3) computed using edgeR and PROPER indicate marginal power values for detecting DEGs at various group sample sizes (e.g., A+B (57) vs C+D (39) marginal power ~0.78 for ≥2-fold changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small groups (e.g., Class A n=10, Class E n=12) have limited power; comparisons involving these groups are exploratory. Mitigation: combine classes or include prior-study samples to increase power; interpret negative findings cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical testing and multiple testing correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Group differences assessed by appropriate tests (t test or Wilcoxon) with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustments for multiple testing; MA smearplots and generalized linear models (edgeR) used with FDR thresholds (FDR <5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate parametric/nonparametric tests depending on data distribution; report adjusted P-values; significance annotation conventions noted (*P<0.05, **P<0.01, ***P<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance rules for pathway/upstream-regulator analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For pathway/upstream regulator analysis, a |z-score| > 2 with P < 0.01 is considered significant (as used in figure legend).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction where appropriate for multiple pathway tests and report directional z-scores and P-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow cytometry and multiplex cytokine analysis standards
rubrics_metrics.description: FACS performed on cryopreserved PBMCs to determine proportions of B cells (CD19+), CD3+CD4+, CD3+CD8+, NK (CD56+), monocytes (CD14+), γδ T cells (TCR γδ+) and intracellular cytokine staining for IFNγ, IL-6, TNF, etc.; cytokine profiling of baseline plasma via multiplex platform (BioRad) including Type I/II IFNs, TNF, IL-1β, IL-6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire samples on BD LSRII; analyze with FlowJo. Determine significance by t tests or Wilcoxon with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment; assess additional markers guided by transcriptomic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic analysis of P. falciparum isolates
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate parasite genetic differences by extracting gDNA from cryopreserved blood pellets at PCR-positive visits and perform P. falciparum genotyping using standard protocols for neutral-loci microsatellite analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control for parasite genetic variation as a potential confounder in host outcome differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine learning and multi-parameter predictive modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use regularized regression methods (lasso, elastic net — preferred) and machine learning algorithms (k nearest neighbors, random forest, linear discriminant analysis) to identify baseline predictors of clinical or sterile immunity from demographic, epidemiologic, erythrocyte variant, parasitological, transcriptomic, FACS, cytokine, and Pf-specific IgG data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elastic net chosen for grouped selection when features >> samples and features are correlated. For algorithms without automatic feature selection, pre-select features using recursive feature elimination. Perform model-specific parameter tuning and repeated k-fold cross-validation to estimate prediction error and select stable, accurate models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model validation, training/test set strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prior-study data to augment sample sizes: reclassify previous samples to current definitions, enabling use of one study as training set and the other as a test set or inclusion of all in cross-validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-validation and independent test data where possible to evaluate generalizability; report cross-validated mean square error and selected feature sets (example: identification of ≥20 parameters from ~8300 features with MSE 0.055–0.060 in simulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional assays for parasite-inhibitory activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess plasma ability to inhibit sporozoite invasion/intrahepatocytic development using a microscale human liver platform and to inhibit blood-stage growth using standardized growth inhibition assays (GIAs) with IgG purified from plasma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect sporozoite entry by anti-PfCSP fluorescence microscopy and quantify exoerythrocytic forms over time; compare baseline plasma from clinically immune, sterilely immune, and susceptible children. Use functional results to infer potential stage-specific mechanisms of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation and integration of functional and serological data
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate parasite-inhibitory activity scores (microscale liver and GIA) with antigen-specific IgG reactivity intensities on the 1,087-antigen microarray using stage-specific combinatorial approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate correlation coefficients and significance values with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for multiple testing; include inhibitory activity scores as parameters in multinomial models for immune outcome and as covariates in Cox models for time-to-first infection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of functional scores in predictive and survival models
rubrics_metrics.description: Include parasite-inhibitory activity scores as additional predictor parameters in multinomial classifiers (clinically immune, sterilely immune, fully susceptible) and as covariates in Cox regression models to assess effects on time-to-first Pf infection or malaria episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally compare accuracy of machine learning algorithms/regression models in selecting variables predictive of parasite-inhibitory activity; interpret effect sizes in survival models and adjust for key covariates (e.g., age).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor, quality control, randomization, and reproducibility practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample processing randomized to ensure equal distribution of classes, covariates, and age among batches; timepoints from same child processed together; thorough documentation of procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make raw data and final processing/analysis scripts publicly available at project conclusion to allow reproduction of analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated problems, limitations, and mitigation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognized limitations include limited power for small-group comparisons (e.g., Class A, E), potential for missing transient T1 blood signals due to 2-week sampling resolution, and possible confounding by co-incident infections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigations: combine immune classes to increase power (A+B vs C+D), incorporate prior-study samples, treat small-group comparisons as exploratory, validate any surrogate markers in controlled human malaria infection studies, and interpret negative results in light of detection limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of sample types and timepoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed sample types and volumes specified per class/timepoint: baseline (May 2011) PBMC, whole-blood RNA, plasma (2 ml), DBS; bi-weekly timepoints: whole-blood RNA, plasma (50 μl), DBS; availability varies by class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified sample types for respective assays (e.g., PBMCs for FACS, whole-blood RNA for transcriptomics, plasma for microarray and functional assays); account for limited volumes in assay planning.
